title: Travel, problems & emergencies
goal: Handle hotels and trains, report a problem or a loss, call for help in an emergency, and talk about conditions with 'if'.
intro:
This unit gives you the language for when things go wrong: losing your bag, a room where the AC doesn't work, a late train, or a real emergency. Learn the emergency phrases (*కాపాడండి!*, help!) by heart.

The grammar is the **conditional**: Telugu makes 'if' with a verb ending, **-తే** (-tē): *వస్తే* (if [someone] comes), *ఉంటే* (if there is). The 'if' clause always comes first.

vocab.note: A budget hotel is often called లాడ్జి (lāḍji).

phrases.en: I need a room for two nights.
The AC in the room isn't working.
Which platform does the train come in on?
I need to make a complaint.

grammar.title: If ... then: the conditional -తే
grammar.body:
Add **-తే** (-tē) to the verb to make an 'if' clause. It is built on the non-past stem, so it is easy to form:
వచ్చు/రా → **వస్తే** (if ... come) · చేయు → **చేస్తే** · వెళ్ళు → **వెళ్తే** · ఉండు → **ఉంటే** · తిను → **తింటే** · ఇవ్వు → **ఇస్తే** · అవు → **అయితే** · పడు → **పడితే**

**If not**: stem + **-అకపోతే**: *రాకపోతే* (if ... doesn't come), *లేకపోతే* (if there isn't; otherwise).

The if-clause comes **first**, and the result can be in any tense or a command. **ఒకవేళ** (in case) at the start makes it more hypothetical. With కావాలి, use **కావాలంటే** (if you want).

examples.en: If it rains, we won't come.

examples.native: మీకు ఏమైనా కావాలంటే నాకు ఫోన్ చేయండి.
examples.roman: mīku ēmainā kāvālaṇṭē nāku phōn chēyaṇḍi.
examples.en: If you need anything, call me.
If the train gets cancelled, let's go by bus.
If we don't leave soon, we'll miss the train.
If I have the money, I'll fly.

grammar.title: Even if, and 'any-': -ఇనా
grammar.body:
**Even if / although**: past stem + **-ఇనా** (-inā): *వచ్చినా* (even if ... comes), *చెప్పినా* (even though ... said), *ఎంత వెతికినా* (however much I searched). **అయినా** alone means 'even so, still'.

The same -ఐనా (-ainā) on question words makes **'any-'** words: ఎవరైనా (anyone), ఏమైనా (anything), ఎక్కడైనా (anywhere), ఎప్పుడైనా (any time, ever). With **-ఓ** they mean 'some-': ఎవరో (someone), ఏదో (something), ఎక్కడో (somewhere).

examples.en: However much I searched, I couldn't find the wallet.
Even if it rains, we'll go.
Is there an ATM anywhere around here?
Someone is knocking at the door.

dialogue.title: The missing bag
dialogue.setting: Emma, a traveller, reports her missing bag to a railway policeman at Vijayawada station.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.native: సార్, నా బ్యాగు కనిపించడం లేదు. ఎవరో తీసుకెళ్ళారు అనుకుంటా.
lines.roman: sār, nā byāgu kanipinchaḍam lēdu. evarō tīsukeḷḷāru anukuṇṭā.
lines.en: Sir, I can't find my bag. I think someone took it.

lines.speaker: Policeman
lines.en: Don't panic. Where did you leave it?

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.native: ఆ బెంచి మీద పెట్టి టికెట్టు కోసం వెళ్ళాను. తిరిగి వచ్చేసరికి లేదు.
lines.roman: ā benchi mīda peṭṭi ṭikeṭṭu kōsam veḷḷānu. tirigi vachchēsariki lēdu.
lines.en: I put it on that bench and went for a ticket. By the time I came back it was gone.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.native: పాస్‌పోర్టు, పర్సు, బట్టలు. పాస్‌పోర్టు పోతే చాలా పెద్ద సమస్య!
lines.roman: pāspōrṭu, parsu, baṭṭalu. pāspōrṭu pōtē chālā pedda samasya!
lines.en: My passport, wallet and clothes. If I lose my passport, it's a huge problem!

lines.speaker: Policeman
lines.native: ఒక్క నిమిషం... ఇది మీదేనా? ఒక ప్రయాణికుడు ఇప్పుడే ఇక్కడ ఇచ్చి వెళ్ళాడు.
lines.roman: okka nimiṣam... idi mīdēnā? oka prayāṇikuḍu ippuḍē ikkaḍa ichchi veḷḷāḍu.
lines.en: One moment... is this yours? A passenger just handed it in here.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.en: Yes, that's it! Thank you so much, sir!

lines.speaker: Policeman
lines.native: లోపల అన్నీ ఉన్నాయో లేదో చూసుకోండి. ఇంకోసారి జాగ్రత్తగా ఉండండి.
lines.roman: lōpala annī unnāyō lēdō chūsukōṇḍi. iṅkōsāri jāgrattagā uṇḍaṇḍi.
lines.en: Check whether everything is inside. Be careful next time.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.en: Definitely. Do I need to write a complaint?

lines.speaker: Policeman
lines.en: No need. As long as everything's there, that's enough.

culture: India's single emergency number is **112** (police 100, ambulance 108, fire 101 still work). Railway stations have a Government Railway Police (GRP) post and the RPF helpline 139. In Andhra and Telangana a 'hotel' is often simply a restaurant, so ask for a *లాడ్జి* or say *ఉండడానికి గది* (a room to stay) when you need accommodation. Strangers are generally quick to help in a crisis: shouting *కాపాడండి!* or *దొంగ!* will draw a crowd fast.
